paragraphs.source_en: So hard to find: a night so still, so hard to find: a hearth so warm, and rarer still, this wordless communion— a pair of lonely souls. No need to scheme, no need to judge. There is no pride, no suspicion, no contempt. Just sit quietly before the hearth, just count in silence the distant alley’s passing watches. Take a sip of plain water, my friend, to moisten your cracked, parched lips. You add a few coal pieces, my friend; the red flame of this fire acknowledges your kindness. On a cold winter night, my friend, people at last begin to cherish hard-won firewood. In this icy world, the hearts of a few, at last, gather into true compassion. Written before March, 1925.

paragraphs.source_zh:
難得，夜這般的清靜，

難得，爐火這般的溫，

更是難得，無言的相對，

一雙寂寞的靈魂！

也不必籌營，也不必評論，

更沒有虛憍，猜忌與嫌憎，

只靜靜的坐對著一爐火，

只靜靜的默數遠巷的更。

喝一口白水，朋友，

滋潤你的乾裂的口唇；

你添上幾塊煤，朋友，

一爐的紅焰感念你的殷勤。

在冰冷的冬夜，朋友，

人們方始珍重難得的爐薪；

在這冰冷的世界，

方始凝結了少數同情的心！

一九二五年三月前作
